title: Building a read-only MCP server on IBM i with RPGLE
author: iNewTech
excerpt: A practical look at using RPGLE, IBM HTTP Server for i, and Db2 for i to expose a controlled, read-only Model Context Protocol server.

sections.heading: Why this project exists
paragraphs: An IBM i developer may know how to inspect a library, program, file, or job, but a chat model cannot see the current state of that partition on its own. MCP4i was started while learning the Model Context Protocol, with a controlled way for an AI client to ask IBM i for read-only information.
This article concentrates on the single-program RPGLE server. The other folders in the repository provide interactive MCP practice with local Ollama and fictional documents.
sections.hinglish: IBM i developer library, program, file ya job inspect kar sakta hai, lekin chat model khud se us partition ki current state nahi dekh sakta. MCP4i AI client ko IBM i se controlled tareeke se sirf read-only information poochne ka example deta hai.

sections.heading: Why use RPGLE for the MCP server?
paragraphs: MCP lets a server advertise tools with names, descriptions, and input schemas, then lets a client list and call those tools through a defined protocol. The IBM i community should be able to study that server-side protocol handling in a familiar language, so the first MCPHTTP.sqlrpgle program handles the MCP request itself instead of sitting behind a Python wrapper.

IBM HTTP Server for i receives POST /mcp and invokes the ILE RPG program as CGI, a pattern IBM documents for RPG programs. The program uses IBM CGI APIs to read the request and write the response, while Db2 for i functions parse and generate JSON. The HTTP server owns the listening socket, so submitting CALL MCP4I/MCPHTTP with SBMJOB would not create a working MCP listener.
sections.hinglish: MCP server ko tool ka naam, description aur input schema batane deta hai; phir client defined protocol se un tools ko list aur call kar sakta hai. IBM HTTP Server for i POST /mcp receive karke ILE RPG program ko CGI ke roop mein chalata hai.

sections.heading: Request flow
paragraphs: The HTTP server receives the request, the RPG CGI program validates and dispatches it, and a fixed Db2 for i query returns a small system-information result. The model never supplies arbitrary SQL.
flow: JSON-RPC result returned to the client
sections.hinglish: Client request bhejta hai, HTTP server RPG CGI program ko invoke karta hai, program request validate karke fixed Db2 read chalata hai aur JSON-RPC result return karta hai.

sections.heading: What the RPGLE source handles
paragraphs: The request handler checks the HTTP method, Origin, content type, and request size before it reads and parses the JSON body. The MCP dispatcher implements initialize, notifications/initialized, ping, tools/list, and tools/call for the 2025-11-25 request-response subset.

During tools/list, the program advertises one tool, get_system_info, with an empty input schema. During tools/call, it accepts only that tool name and runs a fixed read of SYSIBMADM.ENV_SYS_INFO rather than SQL supplied by a model.

The result contains OS and host identity plus a local observation timestamp. Db2 for i escapes the text before the CGI response writer returns it. This is source code ready for a development-partition trial, not a claim that it has already compiled or passed a live IBM i test.
sections.hinglish: Request handler JSON parse se pehle method, Origin, content type aur request size check karta hai. tools/call mein model ka SQL run nahi hota; sirf approved tool aur fixed system read allowed hai.

sections.heading: Deploy the first program on IBM i
paragraphs: The repository deployment guide is the command-by-command reference for copying source to the IFS, creating the library, granting authority, configuring HTTP, and verifying the endpoint. Create the MCP4I library and dedicated MCPJOBQ, MCPJOBD, MCPCLS, and MCPSBS objects using that guide. Then copy MCPHTTP.sqlrpgle to an IFS build directory and compile and bind the program, adjusting the source path for your system.

Add the HTTP configuration directives to a dedicated MCP4I HTTP instance so /mcp maps to the program and the instance uses the new job queue and subsystem. Start the subsystem before the HTTP instance because IBM requires an active subsystem for jobs routed to a custom HTTP job queue. If operations uses SBMJOB, submit STRTCPSVR to an already running control queue rather than submitting the RPG CGI program itself.
sections.code:
CRTSQLRPGI OBJ(MCP4I/MCPHTTP) SRCSTMF('/home/builduser/MCP4i/MCPHTTP.sqlrpgle') OBJTYPE(*MODULE) COMMIT(*NONE) RDB(*NONE) OUTPUT(*PRINT)
CRTPGM PGM(MCP4I/MCPHTTP) MODULE(MCP4I/MCPHTTP) BNDSRVPGM(QHTTPSVR/QZHBCGI)

STRSBS SBSD(MCP4I/MCPSBS)
STRTCPSVR SERVER(*HTTP) HTTPSVR(MCP4I)
sections.hinglish: Pehle library, job queue, job description, class aur subsystem create karo. Phir source ko IFS se compile/bind karo, HTTP configuration mein /mcp map karo, subsystem start karo aur uske baad HTTP instance start karo.

sections.heading: Verify the endpoint safely
paragraphs: The sample endpoint listens only on IBM i loopback, so use the guide's SSH tunnel or run the smoke test from a machine that can reach it. The test covers initialization, tool discovery, one live get_system_info call, and rejection of invalid requests. Keep actual host names and system output out of public logs.
sections.hinglish: Endpoint loopback par listen karta hai. SSH tunnel ya reachable machine se smoke test chalao aur host names ya system output ko public logs mein mat rakho.

sections.heading: Practice the conversation flow with Ollama
paragraphs: If you do not have an IBM i development partition yet, use the completed Python CLI to practise interactive MCP tool calls with local Ollama and sample documents. Its document MCP server, client, and chat entry point show where tool registration, connection, and model interaction happen.

The folder README provides the current uv, Ollama model, and run commands. Python and TypeScript starters let you work through the exercises yourself. These document demos are separate from the RPGLE IBM i server, and their in-memory editing tool is not an IBM i write capability.
sections.hinglish: IBM i partition na ho to local Ollama aur sample documents ke saath Python CLI se MCP tool calls practise kar sakte ho. Yeh demo RPGLE IBM i server se alag hai aur IBM i par write capability nahi deta.

sections.heading: Read-only roadmap and vendor opportunity
paragraphs: The Phase 1 roadmap proposes later tools for library lists, object and file metadata, program references, jobs, source reading, and carefully guarded SQL. Those capabilities are designs, not tools already available from the current RPGLE server.

For IBM i vendors, a supported MCP interface could make product metadata or diagnostics available through narrow tools, but a real offering would also need authentication, tenant boundaries, auditability, performance limits, and a tested release matrix.

For general developers, the learning chapters and local demos provide a way to understand MCP before contributing a client, test, or user experience around IBM i. The next meaningful result is a development-partition compile followed by a client discovering get_system_info and receiving a result checked against that same partition.
sections.hinglish: Roadmap mein metadata, jobs, source reading aur guarded SQL ke ideas hain; current RPGLE server mein yeh tools abhi available nahi hain. Production offering ke liye authentication, auditability, tenant boundaries aur release testing zaroori hain.
